Aditya —

Thanks for the note. Our procurement team confirms the baseline requirements below; our broker is happy to provide a COI and proposed endorsements. Broker contact is policy@underwriters-inc.com (Underwriters Inc.).

Minimums we require for vendors providing hosted services:
- Commercial General Liability: $5,000,000 per occurrence, $5,000,000 aggregate
- Technology/Professional Liability (E&O): $3,000,000 per claim / aggregate
- Cyber Liability: $5,000,000 aggregate (preferred; if not available, we may accept $3M with compensating controls)
- Waiver of Subrogation in favor of BlueCrest is requested where possible
- Additional Insured: BlueCrest Analytics, its affiliates, officers & directors on CGL policy (endorsement required)

We understand E&O endorsements can be limited by market. If Underwriters Inc. can provide proposed wording and a timeline, we'll accept a reasonable endorsement delivery cadence (COI first, endorsement within 30 days) but reserve the right to pause execution if the broker cannot provide endorsement proof within that window.

Looping in legal (legal@bluecrestanalytics.com) to confirm any contract language expectations.

Best,

Hello Susan / Aditya / team —

Thanks for reaching out. Underwriters Inc. can provide a COI and proposed endorsement language. Quick notes:
- We can issue a standard ACORD COI reflecting the requested limits within 3-5 business days once Redwood confirms which named insured entity to list (Redwood Inference, Inc. or Redwood Inference LLC).
- Additional Insured endorsement for CGL is available; we will provide the specific endorsement wording (CG 20 series or equivalent) as a draft.
- Professional/E&O (Tech) policies often do not have an "additional insured" mechanism; where customers request contractual liability coverage we can provide a supplemental endorsement or a letter of coverage confirmation subject to policy terms.
- Cyber endorsements vary by carrier; we will advise whether endorsement or standalone cyber is in force.

Attached: Endorsement_Wording.docx (draft endorsement language) and sample_COI.pdf (carrier sample). Note some carriers include a "to the extent allowed by policy" qualifier — we can flag that to your legal team.

Thanks for the info — looping legal in with suggested approach. Quick legal take / recommended language and acceptance criteria:

1) Naming: We should confirm Redwood entity as "Redwood Inference, Inc." for the COI; BlueCrest should be named as Additional Insured on CGL only (we should avoid trying to force Additional Insured on E&O). Suggested endorsement naming: "BlueCrest Analytics, its subsidiaries and affiliates, and their respective officers, directors and employees."

2) Limits: We can agree operationally to the requested limits for CGL and Cyber. For E&O, confirm whether BlueCrest will accept $3M; if they insist on additional insured on E&O, we should push back and propose a contractual liability carve-out instead.

3) Timing / Delivery: Accept COI at signing provided that (a) COI reflects requested limits, and (b) broker provides written confirmation/endorsement draft within 30 calendar days. If endorsement is not delivered in 30 days, Redwood retains the right to suspend service or withhold credits until resolved.

4) Wording caveat: If broker provides endorsement language containing qualifying language ("to the extent permitted by policy"), Legal will require either carrier confirmation of applicability or a mitigation plan (e.g., escrowed funds or limited credit hold).

I'll redline the MSA section to include the 30-day endorsement delivery term and produce a short addendum clause we can insert into the Order Form. Draft will be attached to this thread within the hour.

Marissa Cole
